inspected_anchors.text: • Basic instrumental variables (IV) regression: Two-stage least squares (2SLS) is provided by ivreg, which separates out the dedicated 2SLS routines previously found in AER. Another implementation is available as tsls() in package sem.
• Binary responses: The LARF (archived) package estimates local average response functions for binary treatments and binary instruments.

• Panel data: Several panel data model packages (see below) provide their own dedicated IV routines for efficient estimation in the presence of high-dimensional data. These include fixest and lfe for fixed effects, and plm for first-difference, between, and multiple random effects methods.
• Miscellaneous: REndo fits linear models with endogenous regressor using various latent instrumental variable approaches. SteinIV provides semi-parametric IV estimators, including JIVE and SPS.

• Regression discontinuity design (RDD) methods are implemented in rdrobust (offering robust confidence interval construction and bandwidth selection), rddensity (density discontinuity testing (also known as manipulation testing)), rdlocrand (inference under local randomization), and rdmulti (analysis with multiple cutoffs or scores).

• Tools to perform power, sample size and minimum detectable effects (MDE) calculations are available in rdpower, while RATest provides a collection of randomization tests, including a permutation test for the continuity assumption of the baseline covariates in the sharp RDD.

When born, animals and humans are thrown into an unknown world forced to use their sensory inputs for survival. As they begin to understand and develop their senses they are able to navigate and interact with their environment. The process in which we learn to do this is called reinforcement learning. This is the idea that learning comes from a series of trial and error where there exists rewards and punishments for every action. The brain naturally logs these events as experiences, and decides new actions based on past experience. An action resulting in a reward will then be higher favored than an action resulting in a punishment. Using this concept, autonomous systems, such as robots, can learn about their environment in the same way. Using simulated sensory data from ultrasonic sensors, moisture sensors, encoders, shock sensors, pressure sensors, and steepness sensors, a robotic system will be able to make decisions on how to navigate through its environment to reach a goal. The robotic system will not know the source of the data or the terrain it is navigating. Given a map of an open environment simulating an area after a natural disaster, the robot will use model-free temporal difference learning with exploration to find the best path to a goal in terms of distance, safety, and terrain navigation. Two forms of temporal difference learning will be tested; off-policy (Q-Learning) and onpolicy (Sarsa). Through experimentation with several world map sizes, it is found that the off-policy algorithm, Q-Learning, is the most reliable and efficient in terms of navigating a known map with unequal states.

A ‘pitch’ may have both musical and linguistic references. As far as music is concerned, ‘absolute ear’ is a commonly ringing phenomenon. In case of the latter, experts who specialize in perfecting linguistic tones to understand language variations will find it an extremely common tool. While many consider relative pitch to be far more important, absolute pitch training has an equal footing in understanding both music and language in general. Postmodernists may not adhere to absolutism but they cannot deny the necessity of the training environment that an absolute ear provides. It serves as a reference to near-perfection for the individual to be able to imitate a determined pitch.   How does absolute pitch training truly benefit? When one can conveniently train in relative pitch, why is there any requirement to train in absolute ear? Relative pitch is more about reconstructing a given tune or composition. Here, a reference note is required in order to position the relative pitch appropriately. If for instance, a singer finds the pre-determined pitch too high or low, they can scale up or scale down to a more convenient pitch. To understand how this is done, the musician should be able to do three things:  Chalk out an appropriate difference between the apparent note and the reference note  Fix proper intervals between the given tones  The ability to pitch a note in the melody of a composition. This is especially expected of singers and the accuracy of the distance between two notes has to be very high.  Already established singers with both relative pitch and absolute pitch training will be able to use their musical abilities to their best. With the right method of training, a seasoned singer will find it easier to transfer their melodic talents to particular instruments. Pitch perfection can be applied to fretless, string instruments such as violin or viola.   Some experts promise better results with relative pitch perfection. Recreating melodies forms the very basis of music, which greatly validates this method of vocal and instrumental training. It is however not true that perfect pitch recognition is futile. For a better understanding of what it is about, you must look at perfect pitch as a landmark that directs you towards the right path. In music, this is your ‘absolute’ or ‘perfect’ point of departure. This phenomenon is greatly applicable to a Capella music, which has practically no reference note, where the essence of the music lies in the singers themselves who create or recreate them.  A guided learning experience must include both listening and speaking. Most experts will tell you that adept listening is the key to mastering the perfect ear. Developing an ear for the right note requires a lot of patience, as it develops only with ceaseless practice. While hiring a teacher is the conventionally accepted method, another better alternative is to go for software training. This allows you access to the pitch correction modules and applications whenever required. Also, this is a one-time investment, unlike tutorials that charge you on a monthly or per sitting basis.  Trying to understand the difference between relativism and absolutism in music and language can be difficult at first. In fact, those who have an absolute ear may not be able to adapt to recognizing changing patterns within different fields of music. Those who experience rigidity in acknowledging relative differences may actually be wrongfully deemed ‘absolute purists who cannot stand tonal varieties.’ The truth lies in the difference between people who can perceive within the 440 Hz range and those beyond that. Also, linguistic and cultural differences apply to both language and music and may pose limitations in understanding how absolutism and relativism applies to both. A question of impending bias towards one’s own culture also comes into the picture, for a person no matter how liberal he is, can never be out of influence of a particular culture.   While absolute ear training can be very useful in certain spheres of music and language, they can also be limiting to the person who is more or less accustomed to only 440 Hz tonal frequency. Imagine if every song were to be played or sung within the aural range, there would be nothing but uniformity! It is important to perceive relativism in conjunction with absolutism for only a balanced outlook will help in a thorough understanding of musical art and communication.   listening-ear-trainer provides online software for relative pitch and absolute pitch training. The absolute pitch training methodology is easily accessible once it has been subscribed for. It includes dozens of exercises for mastering The Singing Funnel Method and The Octave Anchor Pitches Method.

documented_scope: The selected community Synth-for-Stata source identifies version0.0.8 and a Stata13.0 command version declaration; it is not a verified proprietary vendor-native synthetic-control implementation.
Donors default to all panel units except the treated unit; explicitly supplied donor lists require at least two units. Scientific eligibility and spillover exclusion remain caller obligations.
Predictor means ignore missing entries, with all-missing predictor checks. Predictor-specific dates can override the general period; this is not a common balanced measurement window by default.
Default predictor and MSPE periods precede treatment, but explicitly supplied MSPE periods are checked for membership in observed dates rather than for being before treatment.
Help specifies margin0.05 and sigf7; selected command defaults are margin0.005 and sigf12. The mismatch must be retained rather than silently choosing one.

The selected C wrapper assigns pr_loqo status, stores primal weights and returns0 without branching on that status; the header distinguishes optimal, suboptimal, iteration-limit and infeasible states.
RMSPE is computed before a roundmat call alters wsol. The compiled Mata routine body is not inspected, so exact rounding behavior remains unknown.

The nested loss helper maximizes negative squared error. Choosing the larger log objective in allopt is consistent with that sign; a comment saying lower loss does not establish a reversed comparison bug.

README declares GPL>=2, while bundled pr_loqo source/header retains proprietary and commercial-use restriction notices. This is unresolved distribution-rights evidence, not permission to reuse or a legal determination.
Selected returns expose weights, predictor balance, trajectories and RMSPE. General help language about placebo/permutation inference does not qualify a matched inference protocol here.
Upstream integration scripts and saved numerical baselines are inspected author artifacts, not rerun results or independent validation.

content.target: Symbolic P(Y | do(X), Z) for a supplied compatible acyclic latent-confounded graph and observational distribution; no automatic causal discovery or individual counterfactual target.
content.uncertainty: Identification status conditional on the graph/model premises; no fitted effect, confidence interval, posterior or guarantee that the causal graph is true.
content.proposed_route: Retain the original R engine as a symbolic reference and candidate narrow subprocess adapter. Defer direct adoption, embedding and porting until a permissible artifact/environment path and behavioral conformance are established.
conversion_contract: Declare observed node identities and directed versus bidirected edge types separately. Encode a bidirected edge as two opposite igraph edges tagged description="U", preserving parallel edges; check acyclicity on the observed directed graph, not on this encoding.
Require unique names, graph/query membership, disjoint outcome/intervention/conditioning sets and declared causal semantics. Do not silently remove latent tags or infer a DAG from an arbitrary PAG.

For the initial profile use expr=FALSE, steps=TRUE, simp=FALSE, prune=FALSE and stop_on_nonid=FALSE. Empty z selects ID; nonempty z selects IDC. PID, simplification, transport and selection-recovery APIs are separate unqualified profiles.

Parse the structured probability result through a versioned grammar. Preserve bound summation variables, conditioning sets, algorithm, original query and derivation tree; never evaluate a returned LaTeX string as code.

Report identified_formula only after a valid id=TRUE result and validated structured expression. A formula is distinct from a fitted estimate, a confidence interval or validation of the supplied causal graph; conditional support must be checked when evaluating ratios.

Report not_identified only for a completed validated id=FALSE derivation under the declared model class. Retain the tree; do not promise a separately extracted hedge object from this public return without further inspection.

Distinguish invalid graph/query, malformed result, process failure, exhausted resources and cancelled execution from scientific nonidentification. Missing/NULL/empty results without a validated trace are unknown, never numeric zero or a negative certificate.

Preserve exact source/options/input/output hashes, target units and information clock. Any subsequent estimation, numeric support checks and sampling uncertainty need their own qualified method and cannot inherit approval from symbolic ID.

failure_contract.valid_identified: id=TRUE plus validated probability object and derivation
failure_contract.valid_nonidentified: id=FALSE plus completed validated derivation under the selected profile
failure_contract.negative_default: stop("Not identifiable.", call.=FALSE) in the selected public wrapper
failure_contract.suppressed_unstructured: expr=TRUE gives empty string; expr=FALSE gives NULL when steps=FALSE
